## CEO overview

What is changing: Firstmate will report when each delegated task last changed instead of giving every task the time the overall fleet report was produced.
Why it matters: Firstmate Control can use those distinct times to show which work changed most recently, so the captain no longer has to inspect each task separately.
Customer or business impact: The captain can spot recent progress and stale work more quickly, while tasks without trustworthy time evidence remain explicitly unknown instead of receiving an invented order.
Risk and rollout: Low.
  Each task time comes only from its existing status or metadata record, overall report freshness remains separate, and the Control interface is unchanged.
  The existing Recently changed view should begin working automatically after this data reaches it.
  Synchronize this narrative into the live pull request description while preserving its machine-owned `## Pipeline` section.

## What changed technically

- Added `last_changed_at` to each task in `fm-fleet-snapshot.v1`, using the newest readable mtime from its metadata file and status log and returning `null` when neither provides evidence.
- Preserved snapshot-wide freshness in `generated` and `current_state.observed_at` and converted evidenced mtimes to UTC with the platform's BSD or GNU `date` form.
- Added an executable regression with deliberately conflicting metadata and status mtimes that proves independently changed tasks sort in evidence order.
- Updated the stock macOS Bash workflow's expected snapshot assertion count from 18 to 19 after the new regression passed there and exposed the stale count.
- Added `.github/pr-bodies/23.md` as the tracked communication narrative for this pull request.

## Validation

Checks passed: The hosted stock macOS Bash 3.2 job completed all 19 snapshot tests, including the new timestamp regression, before its stale 18-test count assertion failed.
  The other 12 hosted checks passed on target head `24c552673ae89df509ad7c880680420563bdeefe`.
  After the correction, the focused snapshot suite passes 19 of 19 locally, its exact compatibility companion passes 43 of 43 Bearings assertions, the pull request communication suite passes 15 of 15, and the direct assessor accepts this tracked narrative.
  The repository lint gate passes pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0 and all five workflows with pinned actionlint 1.7.12, and the documentation ownership check passes all 77 classified surfaces and 285 local links.
Checks not run: Hosted CI has not run on the unpushed CI-phase correction; the outer executor owns synchronization and final-head hosted verification.
Evidence and limitations: Run `33900144772` shows every snapshot assertion passing on stock macOS Bash 3.2.57 and reports only `expected 18 snapshot/fleet-view tests, got 19`.
  Runs `33900144843` and `33900144862` both reached the communication assessor and reported the same nine missing PR-body fields; in the trusted workflow, the source-of-truth comparison passed before that assessment ran.
  A local Linux host cannot replace the final hosted macOS compatibility run, and filesystem mtimes describe persisted record changes rather than the meaning of events within those records.

## Module-boundary decision

Module-boundary decision: Current module retained.
  Task change time belongs in the existing fleet snapshot producer because that is the shared data source for downstream fleet views.
  The assertion-count correction remains beside the stock macOS compatibility command that owns that test inventory expectation.

## Decision needed

No decision required.
  This preserves the requested timestamp evidence boundary, keeps Control interface work out of scope, and can merge once the outer no-mistakes run confirms the final head is green under the standing authorization.
